text:
Seven games without a win, outscored 29-12, and the conversation in Toronto has moved past the lineup and onto the core. Daily Faceoff Toronto's morning show has Nate Thompson wondering whether "the writing could be on the wall" for Auston Matthews and William Nylander, Nylander has spent the week answering Paul Bissonnette's shots at his effort, and the Leafs Nation staff ran a roundtable titled "Panic Index Edition." Jim Hiller, who used to run the Kings' bench, now gets them on a night his team badly needs anything to go right.

The first change is in net. Anthony Stolarz starts over Sergei Bobrovsky, who had 14 of the 23 starts. Stolarz has been the better goalie this year (+0.8 goals saved above expected in nine games, a .905 save percentage), so this reads less like a rest day than an audition. The trouble is what's in front of him. Toronto had 42% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) over the last five and didn't win the chance battle once. Kirill Marchenko, 14 points in 14 games, is on injured reserve; since he went down Dakota Joshua has played beside Nick Paul and Nylander and Jack Roslovic moved up to the top power play.

The Kings come in from the other direction. They were 1-4-0 in their last five while taking 53% of the chances, and Tuesday's 3-0 win in Boston, with Darcy Kuemper stopping all 29 shots, snapped a four-game skid. Kuemper is still at -5.2 for the season, which is why that shutout mattered. Artemi Panarin (personal) and Trevor Moore are still out; Alex Turcotte has taken Panarin's spot with Alex Laferriere and Adrian Kempe. Kevin Fiala, back from the Olympic injury that cost him nine months, is one assist from 300.

Our numbers give Los Angeles 3.33 expected goals to Toronto's 2.85, and our sleepers are both Kings: fourth-liner Corey Perry (3.5 expected goals in his last 10, 15% to score) and Quinton Byfield, two points from 200 for his career, at 49% for a point. Toronto's playoff chance in our simulations is under 3%.
headline: Toronto turns to Stolarz with seven straight gone
